prompt: Produce exactly one concise natural-language caption (a single sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject, visible actions, and setting. Use specific action verbs and name any clear maneuvers; indicate direction of movement (e.g., toward, past, away from, away toward) and explicitly state whether motions are simultaneous or sequential. Describe body posture with concrete terms (standing, leaning forward/back, seated upright, reclining, crouching, perched) and report facial expressions or gaze only when visually evident (e.g., smiling, frowning, open mouth, eyes looking toward X). Specify whether people or objects are stationary or moving, and if a group appears coordinated describe the formation and coordination (line/row/column/circle, marching in step, striking synchronized poses). Give precise spatial relationships and scale (next to, behind, in front of, atop, a few feet/meters apart), and note interactions with the environment when visible (boarding or disembarking, docked/tied to a pier, leaning on a railing). State the setting type and temporal context only when visually supported (outdoor/indoor, daylight/dusk/night indicated by sunlight, shadows, or artificial lights). Describe surface textures and environmental conditions with observable terminology (calm/rippled/choppy water, wet pavement, puddles, splashes, reflections, motion blur) and report lighting and shadows using visible cues (directional backlight, side light, diffuse/overcast light, strong cast shadows and their direction/length). Keep the caption concrete, image-centered, avoid speculation or subjective judgments unless directly supported by visible evidence, and produce a single clear sentence as the caption.
